item.title: Ideas for execution of a "Monster What Kills You" skip
item.content:encoded:
At some point in the near future (perhaps after the posting of one or more other articles) I would really like to take on the writing challenge of making a "classic monster" skip interesting. It's such a commonly-avoided topic that I can't help but be enticed to try and make it work. Here are some qualities such a hypothetical monster would have to include, as part of the challenge:

  • Very little in the way of motivation, i.e. a predator or something similar
  • Irrepressibly violent tendencies towards humans, i.e. this is just a thing what kills you
  • No cop-outs or deceptions as to its nature, i.e. it is exactly what it seems to be.

Given these constraints, the most plausible avenue to success seems to be setting the monster within a narrative that stands on its own. However, even that feels like cheating to me, as by shifting the focus of the article from the monster to the story, I've effectively conceded that it is simply impossible to make a monster interesting nowadays.

Does anyone know of some modern skips that could provide inspiration? Do you have any ideas about what would be necessary to make this challenge possible? Do you believe it is possible at all? Should I abort this ill-conceived venture at once??? Please let me know.

If it goes well, I might try to do the same for an x-man.

item.title: SCP Reference Help
item.description: I need help to determine if any SCPs exhibit these concepts I have. 6000+ SCPs is a lot to comb through.
item.content:encoded:
I've seen a number of SCPs myself, but not enough. So at the moment there are 2 ideas that might have some potential.

1) An object that can observe past histories

2) A D-class that does not die

.

+ show block
– hide block

With the first, I originally concepted this object being a magnifying glass, however I did note after conception that there's a magnifying glass entry on some knock-off SCP website that refers to themselves as scp classic? Store, cache, preserve? Even if it isn't canon I think my concept can be mixed up a bit more than taking that specific form.

The key element is that this object would be able to reference an edit log for anything that is seen through it. You know, how on some of these posts you can see an edit history? That's the idea, but it could be all contents ever written on a whiteboard. Or in a notebook. But even deeper, say in a long held manuscript; like the Quran, or the Bible. Maybe even ████████ material? Naturally the key to this concept would be in the story surrounding it, but I want to know if this idea exists in the scp lore in anyway. I'm sure people have used time travel in their creation, but this specific trait just might be limiting enough to push a tale.

I do comprehend, being able to see redacted material is a dangerous idea, being that author makes that information unavailable to guide the mystery of it. But if used correctly, it has good potential to revive an old topic. Obviously requires a test of scrutiny.

.

The second concept is a lesser one in which I simply considered: What if there was a D-class that always survived their testing? If we apply this nature to a soldier or a doctor? Sure, there is some possibility, but D-class always gets the worst of it. So again, I want to know if there's any D-class that are SCPs.

This idea has less wiggle room being, at the moment, it's just an entity with writers shield. But there might be some fun to be had with this concept. P.S. I am not thinking of a character trait like Marvel's Darwin, where his body just adapts to any situation. Not my intent what-so-ever. Nor do I wish to pursue some "he's just lucky" trait akin to Domino. What would the D-class be I dunno, but I don't want to start concepting if there's already another similar D-class on the list.

.

If you can help I'd dearly appreciate it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: How to write something in a canon when no one else has heard it before?
item.description: Something I was thinking about after I told a critter told me they weren't aware of the canon my idea would take place in.
item.content:encoded:
I was seeking feedback as well as greenlight for a concept of a tale, and it takes place in the Apotheosis Canon during the 2018 Doomsday Challenge. I assumed a good chunk of members here in the wiki read or at least heard of this canon.

I PM'd a critter and they told me that they weren't familiar with the canon, nor are they interested in reading the canon to provide further critique. As well with other criticism they were able to provide. I told them that I understood and wished them a nice day.

Today I edited my concept around the criticisms I did got and went out seeking feedback again.

So how do I write for a canon that possibly no one else is aware of?

item.title: Can I Get Draft Critique on a Mainlist Rewrite?
item.content:encoded:
Little bit unorthodox, I suppose. I understand that first time authors need two greenlights before posting in the Draft Critique Forum, but the FAQ states that if you have a "successful" (meaning voted positively, I guess?) main list article you can bypass the greenlight process, and go straight to Draft Critique.

So, hypothetically, let's say I wasn't completely happy with an article I posted, and thought about doing a bit of a rewrite; could I post the rewritten draft in the Draft Critique Forum without greenlights, on the basis that the original article is currently positively rated on the main site?

item.title: Help with posting a comment
item.description: I have the mental capacity of a 90 years old to understand modern technology.
item.content:encoded:
First of all: yes, I am ashamed to ask this. However, I prefer to ask before making mistakes.

I'm not a tech savy. Far from it.
Ok, so posting a comment. What kind of help could one possible need with something this simple?

A lot of it, to be honest:

1) what's a heading level 1 (largest)?

2) what's a div block element?

3) what's a clear floats (both)?

4) what's a table wizard?

5) what's a table of contents?

6) what's a code block/ code block wizard?

7) what's a raw text - escape parsing?

8) how do I link another article in my comment?

I am also aware of the Wiki Syntax, and the Advanced Formatting by DrMagnus, however despite my best efforts for the last 2 days to understand what those two try to teach…it's incomprehensible to me.

Lastly, I am mostly reaching out for step-by-step tutorials any of you might know and would be willing to share on formatting. Because I really suck at this whole thing.

Thank you.
